headline: Lets donors deduct gifts to federally chartered veterans' groups even if those groups don't meet the 90% wartime-veteran membership rule.
what_it_does: Before this law, people could only deduct donations to a tax-exempt veterans' group if at least 90% of its members were wartime veterans. This law lets donors deduct gifts to any tax-exempt veterans' group that has a federal charter, whatever share of its members are wartime veterans. Deductions for these gifts are capped at 60% of the donor's adjusted gross income.

who_it_affects.how: They can receive tax-deductible donations even if fewer than 90% of their members are wartime veterans.

who_it_affects.group: People who donate to federally chartered veterans' organizations
who_it_affects.how: They can deduct these gifts on their federal income taxes, up to 60% of their adjusted gross income.
